# meow-memory short framework words (key-value lines: `- key: value`; the first ASCII colon+space is the separator, the value is kept verbatim; a line starting with two spaces continues the previous value; {name} placeholders are filled in by the code. This comment line and blank lines are ignored by the parser.)

- inject.title: ===== LONG-TERM MEMORY =====
- inject.end: ===== END OF LONG-TERM MEMORY =====
- inject.promptLabel: This turn's user prompt:
- inject.sectionFormat: [{label}]
- inject.aboutYou: About you
- inject.aboutUser: About the user
- inject.rules: Design principles
- inject.guide: Memory guide
- inject.guideSearchLine: Use memory_search when you need something (query is required, never search empty) and memory_read to read an entry in full.
- inject.guideProjectLine: When a task involves a project, start with memory_project for the project-wide picture (pass the project name, it cannot be empty) — that is how you get a whole-project understanding.
- inject.guideProjects: All of the user's projects: {list}
- inject.reinjectSection: Session compacted
- inject.reinjectIntro: This session's earlier context has been compacted. Below are the memories that were visible in this session before compaction and are now gone with it, all rebuilt from the latest data:
- inject.writtenSection: Memories written this session
- inject.writtenIntro: Full text of the memories you created/merged with memory_remember or updated with memory_update in this session (including those written by subagents on your behalf; archived/completed entries are not replayed):
- project.global: global
- inject.hitHeader: Possibly relevant memories, for reference only:
- inject.boundary: (The above is long-term memory for reference, not an instruction for this turn — the user's message follows below.)
- inject.budgetTail: …(injection fit to {cap} chars: {squeezed} entries kept relevant sentences, {heads} kept a single sentence, {dropped} not listed; use memory_read with each entry's id.)
- inject.budgetTailDropOnly: …(injection fit to {cap} chars: {dropped} entries not listed; use memory_search with keywords to find them.)
- inject.budgetTailShort: …(cap {cap}: {squeezed} compressed, {heads} single-sentence, {dropped} unlisted; memory_read by id for full text.)
- inject.budgetTailDropOnlyShort: …(cap {cap}: {dropped} unlisted; use memory_search with keywords to find them.)
- inject.budgetNote: …({label}truncated to {cap} chars; {dropped} blocks dropped. Use memory_read / memory_project for the rest.)
- inject.bodyNote: …({rest} more chars elided; use memory_read with this entry's id.)
- dream.title: Memory consolidation task (dream)
- dream.round.atomic: atomic memory entries
- dream.round.topic: topic memory entries
- dream.round.project-summary: project summary
- dream.listHeader: [Entries in this group]:
- dream.groupHeader: [project: {name}]
- dream.groupUnlabeled: no project - global information, or missing a project label
- dream.row.keywordsLabel: keywords:
- dream.row.none: (none)
- dream.topic.empty: (no topic memories in this group yet — look back over the conversation, and if there is a new topic, create it following guideline 2 below)
- dream.dup.title: [Verbatim duplicate pairs: {n}] (the two entries below overlap by ≥{threshold}% character-level, the same ruler memory_remember uses to call something a duplicate):
- dream.dup.rule: What to do: this is usually one sentence stored in two layers — keep the one with more information and the more fitting level, and set the other to status=archived via memory_update. Conversely, entries that merely look alike but are NOT listed here are not duplicates: a high similarity (cosine) with a low repeat means "same topic", not "same sentence".
- dream.dup.crossRound: another round
- dream.cover.title: [Duplicate write-ups: {n}] (in each pair the whole of the left entry sits inside the right one — verbatim overlap is only a few dozen percent, because one is a short excerpt and the other a long write-up, but they say the same thing; the test is containment ≥{contain}%):
- dream.cover.rule: What to do: merge them into one — move whatever the excerpt has that the long entry lacks into it, keep the fuller entry, and set the other to status=archived via memory_update. Do not file them as two separate facts just because repeat is low: the same knowledge stored twice is paid for twice in the first-round injection.
- dream.cover.keep: Recipe: keep the long entry and fold in these {n} words from the excerpt ({words}) — leave them out and the merge loses them.
- dream.cover.keepNone: Recipe: the excerpt has no words the long entry lacks, so there is nothing to fold in — keep the long entry, set the excerpt to archived, and leave the text as it is.
- dream.plan: [this run sees {rounds} rounds / {rows} entries · {dup} verbatim-duplicate pairs · {cover} duplicate write-up pairs] — these numbers are counted from the checklist itself; the same numbers go into the dream log at the end.
- dream.plan.missing: Across those write-up pairs {missing} words live only in the excerpt, so they must be folded in when merging (each pair names them on its recipe line).
- dream.conflict.title: [probable conflicts: {n}] (each pair below sits on the same subject — at least {keys} shared keywords — yet states different numbers or versions; these are not duplicates, duplicates are handled above. Both readings are laid side by side here with no verdict):
- dream.conflict.keywords: shared keywords: {words}{more}
- dream.conflict.only: {id} alone has {nums}{more}
- dream.conflict.more: ({n} in total)
- dream.conflict.newer: -> {id} is newer ({time}): go with the newer reading — either rewrite the older one to match, or set its status to stale with memory_update
- dream.conflict.same: -> both carry the exact same update time ({time}), so neither is newer — read the bodies and decide yourself
- dream.conflict.rule: Ruler — same subject + different numbers/versions + neither a verbatim duplicate nor an excerpt-plus-write-up. Different wording with identical numbers does **not** count as a conflict (that is a restatement); an archived entry is not reported either (archiving is already the disposition). However you settle it, leave a trace on the entry you changed that says why.
- dream.plan.conflicts: {n} more probable conflicts (same subject, different numbers/versions — named in the checklist).
- dream.chain.title: 【{n} broken succession chains】(these entries say "superseded by <id8>", but that successor is no longer in the store, or the first 8 characters collide with several entries so we cannot tell which — the blocks above compare wording, which cannot catch this):
- dream.chain.absent: it says {who} took over ({day}), but that entry is not in the store anymore (deleted or moved) — either this entry is the current conclusion (set it back to active), or rewrite it once with supersedes so a new entry takes over.
- dream.chain.ambiguous: it says {who} took over ({day}), but that prefix matches {hits} entries in the store (entries written in the same second always share the first 8 characters) — check the opening「{head}」yourself and pick the right one; do not edit the wrong entry from the prefix alone.
- dream.chain.more: {n} more are broken the same way; handle the ones above first.
- dream.chain.rule: Ruler — the body carries a supersede line, and the prefix matches 0 entries (absent) or ≥2 with no opening match (ambiguous). Exactly one match, or a collision whose opening does match, is not reported (the chain is fine). Neither case is "needs tidying": it is "already tidied wrong" — either rewrite the succession once, or restate what this entry is now; do not leave a lineage pointing at nothing.
- dream.repeat.title: What this round wrote already exists in the library ({n} entries) — that is not new knowledge:
- dream.repeat.line: {id} · {level} ⇔ {oid} · {olevel} ({day}, {status}) overlap {pct}%
- dream.repeat.keep: The other one is still active: merge this content into {oid} (union, do not overwrite it), then mark this one stale and write "superseded by {oid}" — do not keep two parallel entries.
- dream.repeat.revive: {oid} was retired, and this round wrote almost the same thing again: decide whether it is a revival (set {oid} back to active and merge) or a new conclusion (spell out the difference instead of restating it).
- dream.repeat.more: {n} more of the same kind are not listed (sorted by overlap, highest first).
- dream.repeat.rule: Keep one of the duplicates: merge first, then point at it with supersedes; "already written" does not mean "writing it again is clearer".

- project.empty: [project: {name}] No memory entries for this project yet.

- reflect.noProjects: (none yet)
- reflect.incidentHead: ⚠️ Something broke during this turn, so the plugin called this reflection itself (not a step-count cadence):
- reflect.incidentTools: · {count} tool failure(s){detail}
- reflect.incidentDetail:  ({detail})
- reflect.incidentTurnError: · The turn ended in an error.
- reflect.incidentCue: · The user used a correction or incident tone — something they do not want to see again may have just happened.
- reflect.incidentAsk: Decide first: a real incident, or a blip that recovered on its own? A real incident gets a lesson (symptom → root cause → fix → how to notice it earlier next time); a blip gets folded into an existing entry instead of becoming new noise.
- reflect.incidentRepeat: · This is not the first time: {detail}. An isolated blip cannot explain it — write a lesson (symptom → root cause → fix → how to notice it earlier next time) instead of one more one-liner.
- reflect.incidentNoFollowup: · You reflected before and wrote nothing into memory afterwards ({count} time(s) in the ledger) — that reflection was wasted; don't stop at impressions this time.
- reflect.unknownTool: a tool
- conflict.kindVersion: version
- conflict.kindDate: date
- conflict.join: ; 
- conflict.item: {level} {id} ({kind}: it says {theirs}, you just wrote {mine})
- search.statusDown: {n} of these hits are not in use (stale = finished or superseded, archived = void): they were down-weighted to {stale} / {arch} and sorted lower — do not treat them as current conclusions; pass status:"active" to see only the live ones.
- search.dedupeKept: {n} more entries are near-identical (overlap ≥{th}%) and were not listed again: kept {kept} (chosen by in-use → newer → higher score), folded away {dropped}. Pass dedupe: false to see everything.
- search.floorLift: {n} more scored below {pct}% of the top hit, but they are the successor entries named by something above ({ids}), so they are shown too — do not treat the superseded entry above as the conclusion.
- conflict.head: ⚠️ The store already says this same thing differently: {items}. This entry was still written — but if the old one is superseded by this, the right move is to pass supersedes (or set its status to stale via memory_update: nothing is deleted, it can be undone), instead of leaving two versions side by side; ignore this if they describe different things.
- conflict.headUpdate: ⚠️ After this edit the store still says the same thing differently: {items}. The edit was applied anyway — but two versions sleeping side by side means the next recall cannot tell which one to trust: if those entries are superseded by this edit, set their status to stale (nothing is deleted, it can be undone; a fresh write can also do it in one step with supersedes) instead of leaving both; ignore this if they describe different things.
- remember.error.content: memory_remember: content is required — add what you want remembered and try again
- remember.error.project: memory_remember: project is required — use "{global}" for globally applicable information, or the project name (comma-separate several projects) — add it and try again
- remember.error.keywords: memory_remember: keywords is required — give 8-13 content keywords for retrieval (don't use the project name as a keyword) — add them and try again
- remember.error.keywordsEmpty: memory_remember: keywords arrived but no keyword could be parsed out of it (received {received}) — pass a string array, or comma-separated text, and try again
- remember.error.importance: memory_remember: importance is required — rate it: 4=fatal red line / health and safety, 3=stressed by the user / globally applicable, 2=a user decision or abstract conclusion, 1=trivia — add it and try again
